description: CrowdSec enforcement inventory, detection activity and pipeline health. Active decisions are not requests blocked. Simulation triggers are not bans. All agent metrics are aggregated; shared LAPI gauges are deduplicated.

panels.title: Protection now · live inventory and replica health
Local enforced decisions
panels.description: Local/manual decisions currently eligible for enforcement. Excludes simulation and community lists. A decision can cover a range; this is not a unique-IP or blocked-request count.

panels.title: Community / imported bans
panels.description: Shared LAPI database gauges deduplicated across replicas. These bans can exist while local decision count is zero.

panels.title: LAPI replicas · expected 2
panels.description: Scrape availability, not proof of end-to-end enforcement. Both replicas should be available.

panels.title: AppSec replicas · expected 2
panels.description: Scraped AppSec instances. Both should be available.

panels.title: Agent coverage · % ready
panels.description: Ready agents divided by desired agents, including nodes missing from Prometheus.

panels.title: Decision inventory
panels.description: Read-only decision feed. If unavailable, empty IP tables mean unknown, not no bans.

options.content:
**Active decision ≠ blocked request.** A scenario trigger may only produce a simulated alert. Cowrie is configured for immediate decisions; the tarpit scenario is simulated. Traefik applies IP decisions to protected HTTP services; Cowrie remains accessible.

The tables below show **current local/manual enforcement decisions**, refreshed within roughly 60 seconds. Empty rows are meaningful only when **Decision inventory = CURRENT**. Open **Active decisions · local UI** for management and **CrowdSec Console** for cloud reporting.

panels.title: Who has a decision · expiry and recent observations
Active local decisions · expires at
panels.description: Current read-only LAPI bouncer inventory; simulated decisions never appear. Up to 1,000 newest local/manual decisions. Expiry is derived from the remaining duration, not issue time. This table is always current regardless of dashboard time range.

panels.title: Time remaining · local decisions
panels.description: Same current decisions as the expiry table. Bouncer refresh can delay enforcement or removal. No inference about when the ban was issued.

panels.title: Inventory age
panels.description: Age of the last successful LAPI response. No data means unknown.

panels.title: Rows omitted by limit
panels.description: Above zero: table is truncated to 1,000 newest local decisions. Use the local UI for complete inventory.

panels.title: All active decisions · origin / reason / action
panels.description: Shared database counts deduplicated across LAPI replicas. Includes community blocklists; not traffic counts.

panels.title: Decision history · observed and removed
panels.description: Observation history from the inventory poller, starting with this deployment. observed = first seen during polling; snapshot = already present when exporter started; removed = no longer returned by LAPI. These are observation times, not exact issuance or unblock times. No events is normal when decisions have not changed.

panels.title: Detection · activity does not necessarily create a ban
Scenario triggers / second · includes simulation
panels.description: Overflows indicate detection activity. Profiles, allowlists, and simulation determine whether a decision follows.

panels.title: Scenario triggers · selected time range
panels.description: Includes simulation. Counter increases are estimated over the selected range, not a count of active bans.

panels.title: Log pipeline · all agents, with source-level failures
Lines read / second · by source
panels.description: Acquired lines across every agent. A flat Cowrie source despite new honeypot sessions indicates stalled ingestion.

panels.title: Unparsed lines / second · by source
panels.description: Includes application diagnostics that are not access logs. Investigate changes in access-log parsing, not the percentage alone.

panels.title: Sources · lines read in selected range
panels.description: Each agent and source, including Cowrie logship when acquisition is active.

panels.title: Events reaching scenarios / second
panels.description: Proves events reached detection buckets after parsing and allowlists. Does not imply a ban.

panels.title: Enforcement components · AppSec and Traefik polling
AppSec requests / second
panels.description: Traffic reaching each AppSec replica. Rule hits and decisions are different measurements.

panels.title: AppSec blocked requests / second
panels.description: AppSec-reported blocked requests. Does not count Traefik IP-decision blocks.

panels.title: Traefik decision polling / second
panels.description: Polling proves connectivity, not enforcement. Stream mode does not expose per-request allow/deny totals here; use the VPN regression test to verify external blocking.

panels.title: Live scrape targets · all components
panels.description: Scrape status for each discovered target. Missing agents are also detected by the desired/ready coverage stat at the top.

panels.title: Investigation · recent engine warnings and errors
CrowdSec warning / error logs
panels.description: Engine errors can explain flat detections despite healthy pod status. Selected time range applies.

panels.title: UDM edge bouncer · perimeter L3/L4 (the only CrowdSec cover for non-Traefik ports)
IPs blocked at the edge
panels.description: Current IPs in the UDM nftables set (crowdsec + CAPI origins; cowrie excluded to keep the honeypot alive).

panels.title: ipset fill ratio
panels.description: Capacity used (0-1). Approaching 1 means decisions are being dropped — see the drop counter.

panels.title: UDM memory available
panels.description: Free memory on the gateway. The bouncer sizes its ipset against this.

panels.title: Decisions dropped (cap)
panels.description: Cumulative decisions dropped because the ipset was full. Non-zero => the edge cannot hold the feed; tighten the mirror filter or raise the cap.

panels.title: Edge set size over time
panels.description: Blocked IP count trend. A cliff to zero means the bouncer lost the mirror feed.

panels.title: AbuseIPDB reports from the edge (by status)
panels.description: UDM-side AbuseIPDB uploader, if enabled. NOTE: this is DISJOINT from the in-cluster cowrie reporter (which reports honeypot attackers the edge never sees).

panels.title: IPs Reported to AbuseIPDB (24h)
panels.description: Cowrie attackers submitted to AbuseIPDB by the daily reporter CronJob. 0 outside the daily run window is normal.

panels.title: AbuseIPDB Report Failures (24h)
panels.description: Failed AbuseIPDB submissions (rate-limit / policy rejection). Should be 0.

panels.title: AbuseIPDB Reporter Log
panels.description: Daily reporter output: which IPs reported + resulting confidence score, and skip counts.
